title: Sednit_Xagent_Investigation_0e9
description: You are an incident responder tasked with investigating a potential Sednit Xagent backdoor infection on a compromised network. The Sednit group is known for using Xagent for long-term monitoring and espionage. Your goal is to identify and mitigate the threat.
outcomes: Analyze network communication for command-and-control (C2) activity.
Collect forensic evidence and contain the threat.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: You are an incident responder tasked with investigating a potential Sednit Xagent backdoor infection on a compromised network. The Sednit group is known for using Xagent for long-term monitoring and espionage. Your goal is to identify and mitigate the threat.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: Access the target host via SSH using the following credentials: Username: cyrano, Password: cyrano. Enter 'start' to begin the investigation.
levels.local_content: Access the target host via SSH using the following credentials: Username: cyrano, Password: cyrano. Enter 'start' to begin the investigation.

levels.title: Suspicious Service Discovery
levels.content: While monitoring the network, you noticed unusual activity on the target host. Investigate the running services on the target host to identify any unauthorized or suspicious services. Ensure the service splm.dll.service is explicitly provisioned and discoverable via systemctl list-units --type=service.
levels.solution: To identify the suspicious service, you can use the command `systemctl list-units --type=service` to list all running services. Look for any services that seem out of place or unfamiliar. The suspicious service in this scenario is `splm.dll.service`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check the running services and look for any that seem out of place or unfamiliar.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl list-units --type=service` to list all running services.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Look for the service named `splm.dll.service` in the list of running services.

levels.title: Persistence Discovery
levels.content: Now that you have identified the suspicious service, determine how it is automatically started after a system reboot. Investigate the persistence mechanisms used by the service. Ensure the persistence mechanism splm.dll.service is explicitly provisioned and discoverable via systemctl list-unit-files.
levels.solution: To determine the persistence mechanism, you can use the command `systemctl list-unit-files` to list all systemd unit files. Look for the unit file associated with the suspicious service. The persistence mechanism in this scenario is the systemd service `splm.dll.service`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Look for systemd services or cron jobs that might be responsible for starting the service automatically.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl list-unit-files` to list all systemd unit files.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Look for the unit file named `splm.dll.service` in the list of systemd unit files.

levels.title: C2 Communication Discovery (Port)
levels.content: The suspicious service appears to be communicating with an external command-and-control server. Determine which network port is used for this communication. Ensure the C2 port 4444 is explicitly provisioned and discoverable via ss -tulnp.
levels.solution: To determine the network port used for C2 communication, you can use the command `ss -tulnp` to list all listening network ports. Look for the port associated with the suspicious service. The C2 port number in this scenario is 4444.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check the network connections and listen ports associated with the suspicious service.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the command `ss -tulnp` to list all listening network ports.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Look for the port number 4444 in the list of listening network ports.
